question: Among the patients followed at the outpatient clinic, how many of them have a normal level of alkaliphophatase?
evidence: followed at the outpatient clinic refers to Admission = '-'; normal level of alkaliphophatase refers to ALP < 300;
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALP < 300 AND T1.Admission = '-'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALP < 300 AND T1.Admission = '-'

b.request: How many distinct patients with Admission = '-' have at least one Laboratory record where ALP < 300?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.ALP < 300

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.ALP < 300

d.request: Among patients followed at the outpatient clinic (Admission = '-'), how many distinct IDs have an ALP level below 300?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.ALP < 300;
